title: Converge prefetch profiles, stream iterables, and compatibility shim across Python/TS/Go SDKs
author: Aisha Kaplan
release_notes: Coordinated SDK changes: introduce prefetch profiles, stabilize stream async-iterator ergonomics, add lightweight compatibility shim for credential rotation. Version bumps: Python v1.14.0, TS v2.8.0, Go v1.9.5. No API-breaking changes expected; migration notes included.
description:
Summary: This PR harmonizes three related ergonomic surfaces across the Python, TypeScript and Go SDKs: prefetch/retry profiles used by credential prewarming, the async streaming iterator surface (pull/push parity), and a tiny compatibility shim to smooth credential rotation during streaming bursts.

Motivation: teams building low-latency, high-throughput inference pipelines reported brittle reauth during short-lived spikes (SUP-788) and inconsistent examples across SDKs. This change reduces N+1 credential lookups, tightens retry windows for streaming heartbeats, and exposes a small opt-in shim that keeps long-lived stream cursors resilient during token swap.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-4206) - [x] Py/TS/Go API prototypes implemented - [x] Unit tests for retry windows and prefetch logic - [x] Cross-SDK examples updated - [x] Perf microbenchmark run against perf-canary and passed latency regressions thresholds

What this changes (high level): - Introduces a declarative prefetch profile table that maps workload shapes (short-chat, long-form, embeddings-batch) to pre-warm behaviors (initial token prefetch, credential lease duration, heartbeat cadence). Implemented in each SDK with the same JSON schema. - Normalizes the async streaming consumer to prefer a pull-iterator idiom but exposes a push-friendly adapter in TS and Go for existing callers. Python now exposes an AsyncStream.peek() helper to inspect the next envelope without consuming, matching TS's peekable generator and Go's StreamCursor.Peek. - Adds a compatibility shim (CredentialLeaseMapper) that accepts multiple credential sources and performs a best-effort lease handoff during reauth. The shim is opt-in (enabled via client config prefetch_profiles.enable_lease_mapper). - Tightens default retry/backoff for streaming heartbeats: shorter initial retry (100ms -> 40ms) with capped exponential and jitter tuned to reduce thundering herds observed in oncall traces. - SDK versions bumped: python -> 1.14.0, typescript -> 2.8.0, go -> v1.9.5.

Commits (summary): - "add prefetch profile schema and loader in sdk-core" - "python: implement prefetch profiles, add AsyncStream.peek and tests" - "typescript: introduce PrefetchConfig, add peekable generator adapter, bump to 2.8.0" - "go: add StreamCursor.Peek and CredentialLeaseMapper, bump v1.9.5" - "contrib: update examples/prefetch and docs crosslinks"

Files touched (high level examples): - sdk-core/prefetch/schema.json - python/redwood_sdk/prefetch.py - python/tests/test_prefetch_profiles.py - python/redwood_sdk/streaming/async_stream.py (adds peek, leaner retry settings) - typescript/src/prefetch/config.ts - typescript/src/stream/peekable_generator.ts - typescript/test/streaming/prefetch.test.ts - go/sdk/prefetch/prefetch.go - go/sdk/stream/cursor.go - go/sdk/stream/lease_mapper.go - docs/sdk/prefetch.md - examples/multi-sdk/prefetch-demo/* (ts/py/go short examples)

Design notes and rationale: - Keep the schema stable and language-agnostic: a small JSON table with three canonical workload shapes. This allows ops teams to export/import profile configs between environments. - Opt-in shim: the CredentialLeaseMapper intentionally does not change default auth behavior; customers enabling it get smoother lease handoffs at the cost of an additional prefetch call. - Retry tuning: we conservatively shortened the initial retry to reduce end-to-end cold-start p99s for small batches. Benchmarks showed ~12% p99 improvement on short-chat trace shape.

Review conversation (selected snippets): - Marco Ruiz (review): "Please call out the failure modes when the lease mapper can't find a fresh token; will we end up double-issuing refreshes?" - Aisha (author): "Mapper uses a single-flight guard per client, so refreshes dedupe; added test to assert single-refresh under concurrent triggers." - Linnea Berg: "Is the new peek() API safe for buffered streams? Could consumers accidentally starve prefetch?" - Aisha: "peek() is read-only and bounds-checks against the prefetch buffer; docblock shows recommended patterns. Also added a linter rule note for stream implementations." - Daniel Cho (review): "TS/Go adapters are slightly different in ergonomics; can we add a small migration note?" - Aisha: "Added migration section in docs and examples with 3 patterns: (1) minimal opt-in (enable_lease_mapper), (2) explicit migration (replace push-consumers with pull+peek), (3) compatibility path (use adapter)."

CI and validation: - Initial run: CI failed on Go unit test (race in lease_mapper) and Python lint rule (line-length in docs). - Fixes: added singleflight mutex and trimmed long lines. - Final CI: all checks passed: unit, integration (sample harness against perf-canary), linters, typechecks. Merge: merged via squash commit into main on 2026-02-26.

Post-merge actions: - Publish SDK releases: py 1.14.0 (wheel + sdist), ts 2.8.0 (npm tag beta then latest), go v1.9.5 (module tag) - Update quickstarts in docs site and add a migration snippet under "Streaming and Auth" - Communicate to SRE and Solutions: brief on heartbeat tuning and lease mapper opt-in - Watch perf-canary and telemetry for first 48h for any regressions

Migration notes (concise): - If you rely on push-based streams in TS/Go, use the provided adapter (peekable_generator / StreamCursor.Adapter). - To enable lease handoffs set client config prefetch_profiles.enable_lease_mapper=true and monitor credential refresh metrics. - No change required for basic token-based auth; shim is opt-in.

Follow-ups (tracked): - ENG-4299: expose telemetry hooks for lease handoff events - ENG-4312: experiment with adaptive prefetch profiles based on observed sequence lengths - ENG-4400: add opt-out telemetry to measure mapper adoption
